Faceless studio · reference study · 6 September 2026

Devices in a WordPress Documentary

Coding with Lewis, “WordPress Is Eating Itself Alive”, uploaded 1 September 2026, 34:48, 207k views. A talking-head documentary that cuts to a device every few seconds. The first sixteen minutes were framed at one frame a second and nine devices were burst at ten to twenty frames a second to read how they move. Every frame below is from the video.

The channel does not invent motion. Almost every device is a real artefact (a page, a screen, a headline, a dashboard) pushed into slowly by the camera while one thing on it changes: a number counts, a line is highlighted, a cursor clicks, a word is typed. That is the same principle our documents-as-footage rule came from, taken further.

The shape of the video

MeasureValueNote

Talking head share (first 16 min)about a third of framesthe rest is devices
Camera on a devicealmost always movinga slow push of 5 to 15% over 2 to 4 s, so a static screenshot never sits still

Sound was measured as energy jumps over 21 dB in 30 ms against the cut list from ffmpeg scene detection. It confirms your ear: clicks on some scene changes. Typing sounds under typed text could not be separated from speech by this method; taken from your note.

Devices, one by one

Real page, pushed in, one line highlighted

we have this

A blog post or web page at full width, the camera pushing in slowly, a yellow marker highlight over the sentence being read. In the longer posts the highlight grows line by line as the narration reaches each line.

Marker: hard-on, yellow, the highlighted words turn link-blue. Push: about 8% over 3 s.

Proposal 1. Our document scene uses a gold sweep on one line. Add a marker variant: yellow, hard-on per line, growing line by line with the words, and give every document a slow push. ~2 h.

Number counting inside a sentence

we have part of it

The figure in a quoted sentence counts up in place while the rest of the sentence stands still; then the page jumps to a second excerpt with the final number boxed in orange.

78,330 to 100,000 in 1.4 s at ten updates a second, blue digits; the orange box lands hard.

Proposal 2. Our keyword figures count up over footage; this puts the count inside the document's own line. Add a count-up to the document scene's highlighted figure, with an optional orange box. Same as ledger proposal 5. ~2 h.

Dashboard counter, then the camera dives into the number

new to us

A real analytics panel counts its downloads figure; after 2.6 s the camera pushes into the number and the count continues for another 4 s until it lands.

290 to 46,676 over 7 s; changing digits carry motion blur; the push is about 3x.

Proposal 3. A dashboard card template (label, big figure, sub-label, date range) with a count that outlasts a push-in. Good for our .gov statistics pages where a figure sits in a table. ~3 h.

Giant glowing counter on a texture

we have part of it

A figure alone on a dark or textured ground, green or white glow, stepping up in hard jumps with a unit label under it.

116,998 to 160,000; 100,745 to 4,761,456 INSTALLS in four hard steps 1.5 s apart.

Proposal 4. Our stat card counts in a corner. Add a full-frame stat variant: one figure, one unit, glow, hard steps for a series of values. ~2 h.

Cursor that clicks a real button

new to us

A real interface (the WordPress update screen, a download page) with a pointer gliding to the button and clicking, the page pushing in as it does.

Pointer travel ~0.3 s, then a 2 s push; the click is one of the sounded cuts.

Proposal 5. A cursor layer for document scenes: a pointer that travels to a named element and clicks, with a click sound. Captures already know where the quoted element is. ~3 h.

Typing into the document

we have part of it

A quotation is typed into the page itself, cursor blinking, at about 55 ms a character, while the camera pushes into the line being typed.

Someday, right? typed in 0.85 s; push about 2x over 2 s; cursor blinks for 1 s after.

Proposal 6. Our typewriter runs in a column over footage. Add typing INTO a document scene, at the quoted line's position, with the push. ~2 h.

Dated year stamp on footage

we have this

A small year in the corner of archival footage: 2003, 2010, 2018, 2022/3.

Bottom-right, small, mono, present on the cut.

Dated headline card

we have part of it

A date as a heading with the source's own headline and a line of the post under it, on the post's ground.

Hard-on with the cut, then the push.

Proposal 7. Our dated slug is a stamp; this is a card. Add a headline card: date, headline, source line, on a document ground. ~1.5 h.

Version labels swapping on a flat ground

we have this

WordPress 1.2 becomes 1.3, 1.4, 1.5 on a pink ground, the number in blue, one hard swap per version.

Swaps 0.5 to 1 s apart; the card drifts slightly.

Wordmark morph

new to us

The WordPress wordmark glitches between four historical typefaces and settles with a subtitle.

Four glitch bursts of ~0.3 s over 4.4 s; the ground stays white.

Proposal 8. A glitch-morph between two versions of a name or a figure (the old wordmark to the new; the old fee to the new). Fits a correction beat. ~3 h.

Entity cards and a system map

new to us

White cards with an icon and a bracketed role, WORDPRESS [SOFTWARE], WORDPRESS.ORG [STRUCTURE], WORDPRESS FOUNDATION [LEGAL], AUTOMATTIC [PROFIT], then nodes joined by lines into an organisation chart while the previous layer dims.

Nodes appear 0.3 s apart with a fade and a small scale; connectors draw over 0.3 s; the earlier layer drops to 30%.

Proposal 9. A relations card: two to six named boxes, connectors that draw on the word, the previous layer dimming. Exactly what a rule video needs to show who sets a rule and who enforces it. ~4 h.

Person card

new to us

A photo, a name, a role, then a list of roles with dates.

Card hard-on, list lines 0.4 s apart.

Proposal 10. A person card from a public photo and a verified role list. Needs a photo we have the right to use, so mostly officials with public-domain portraits. ~2 h.

Line chart drawing to its endpoint

new to us

A curve draws on a dark ground; the endpoint value follows the line and lands as a label.

Draw over ~3 s; the label tracks the tip.

Proposal 11. A chart card: line or bars from a small table, drawn on the word, endpoint labelled, source under it. Our data comes from .gov tables already. ~4 h.

Mocked app screen as a prop

not for us

A banking app balance rising to $29,500,000 to illustrate a funding round.

Count over 2 s on a phone UI.

Giant headline bleeding off the frame

new to us

A news headline in huge black serif, deliberately larger than the frame so words are cut at the edges, the camera drifting across it.

Two lines visible; drift about 5% over 2 s.

Hand-drawn annotation

new to us

An arrow drawn onto the page pointing at the word being discussed.

Drawn on over ~0.4 s.

Proposal 12. Same as ledger proposal P6: a marker arrow or circle on a document scene. ~2 h.

Error page and placeholder as props

new to us

A real 503 page, a real “we’re unable to show this content” card for a deleted post.

Present on the cut, pushed in.

Split panels for a dispute

not for us

Two speakers in stacked panels for a back-and-forth.

Talking-head material; our channel has no faces.

Code and old interfaces as texture

we have this

Cascading code panels, Windows-era screenshots, a network of W logos.

Panels 0.3 s apart; screenshots pushed in.

The two you pointed at

Both were missed in the first pass. Burst at ten frames a second, here is what they do.

Quote zoom: the sentence on screen, then the key phrase fills the frame

new to us

A quotation set large on a near-black ground (or the real filing in its own serif), shown as a WINDOW wider than the frame so lines bleed off both edges. The key phrase carries a hard blue box. The camera does not travel smoothly: it cuts from window to window as the reading moves, each window held 1.3 to 4 s with a slight drift, and on the important phrase it pushes in until that phrase alone fills the frame. On the filing, the line being read is sharp and the lines above and below are blurred, a focus band about two lines high.

1175 s: “a cancer to WordPress” boxed, 1.3 s, then a jump to “unchecked, cancer will spread” boxed, held 4 s. 1243 s: the filing pans paragraph to paragraph in 1 to 2 s jumps with the focus band, then zooms to “a cheap knock-off” at roughly six times the page scale. 716 s: a strobe of text close-ups at five cuts a second.

Proposal Q. A quote scene for us: the quotation typeset in our type on an ink ground, or the captured document itself, opened as a window wider than the frame; a gold box lands hard on the marked phrase on its spoken word; the camera cuts between windows as the reading moves and pushes into the marked phrase until it fills the zone; a focus band on documents. We already know where the quoted line is on every capture. ~5 h. The strobe is a separate, cheaper device: ~1 h.

Phrase build with a size hierarchy (your WhatsApp clip)

we have part of it

Every spoken word appears in place with a soft fade of about 0.2 s, in the order spoken, grouped into rows by phrase; the emphasised word is set about 1.6 times larger and the payoff word is yellow; the block clears on the cut to the next still, and each still pushes in slowly. Rounded bold sans with a dark stroke, upper third of a 9:16 frame.

12 s clip, three stills. “Everyone tells you to never” builds word by word over 1.0 s, “Give up” lands larger at 1.1 s and the block holds 1.3 s to the cut. The misalignments you saw: each phrase row is placed by hand, so “Give up” sits off the axis, “THAT / is bad advice” and “That / Dont / Work” stack unevenly, and “Successful” fades before “people” arrives.

Proposal B. Our spoken line already lands every word on its own timing; this adds a size and colour hierarchy per word (*^ ... *!word* ... *) and phrase rows on a fixed grid, so nothing is placed by hand and the rows stay on one axis. Clears on the cut. Best over stills and generated images, and the natural caption mode for Shorts. ~3 h.

What this changes in our thinking

  • Everything moves, gently. Not one screenshot sits still. A 5 to 15% push over the shot is the baseline. Our document scenes drift vertically; the push is missing.
  • The artefact is the graphic. Counters live inside dashboards and sentences, highlights live on the page, typing happens in the post. Fewer invented cards, more real surfaces with one live element.
  • Sound marks entrances. Clicks on device entrances (measured at roughly twice chance), typing under typed text, presumably a tick under counters. Our masters are silent under type.
  • The system map. Entity cards joined into a chart is the clearest way this video explains who owns what. Our rule videos need the same for who writes, who enforces, who pays.
